title: SLO-driven fidelity degradation notes
summary: Working notes for an SLO-first approach to graceful degradation: map SLOs to fidelity tiers (model variants + quantization + batching), enforce via control-plane policies, and implement progressive regional spillover. Purpose: reduce outage blast radius while preserving critical user journeys and predictable unit cost.
body:
Context:
- Problem: we need predictable app-level SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency and availability) across hosted/dedicated/private deployments when capacity or region failures occur. Current reactive fallbacks are patchy: some routes drop to tiny models, others time out, and ops run ad-hoc scripts.
- Goal: codify an operator-friendly, SLO-driven fidelity ladder that control plane can enforce automatically with observable guardrails.

Key principles (high level):
1) SLO-first: define per-route SLOs and map each SLO to an ordered list of fidelity states (full, reduced-cache, quantized-variant, async-queue, graceful-empty/placeholder). Always prefer a safe lower-fidelity response over timeouts.
2) Tiered capacity awareness: keep soft- and hard-thresholds (utilization, queue depth, tail latency) for each capacity pool (region, reserved, burst). Use these thresholds to trigger progressive fidelity transitions.
3) Regional spillover with intent: prefer intra-region hedges, then cross-region failover on compatible model families, with explicit cost/regulatory tags.
4) Predictable cost impact: every fidelity transition should have an estimated per-token cost delta recorded so product teams can understand economics.
5) Observability and fast reversal: every transition is annotated in traces, emits an event to the console, and auto-rolls back if SLOs return to normal in N minutes.

Fidelity ladder (example mapping for chat-generation route with SLO 300ms p95):
- Level 0: full model (gptx-std-32b, 16-bit, caching enabled, batching size auto). Expected p95: 150-250ms. cost: high.
- Level 1: variant w/ smaller kv cache but same model topology (gptx-std-32b, reduced-kv, 16-bit). Expected p95: 200-300ms. cost: ~-10%.
- Level 2: quantized variant (gptx-std-32b-q4), dynamic-batching aggressive. Expected p95: 250-350ms. cost: ~-40%.
- Level 3: model family fallback (gptx-medium-8b, q4), cache warmup heuristics. Expected p95: 300-450ms. cost: ~-70%.
- Level 4: async proxy (enqueue request, return 202 + polling) for non-critical paths.
- Level 5: graceful placeholder (short canned reply / degradation message) for user journeys that must not block UX.

Trigger signals (examples):
- Pool CPU/GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 30s => consider Level+1 for best-effort routes.
- p95 latency crossing SLO for 2 consecutive windows (1m windows) => escalate fidelity for that route only.
- Error budget burn rate > 2x forecast => global partial degrade to Level 2 across non-SLA customers.
- Region partition detected (control-plane heartbeat missing > 45s) => failover policy activates region spillover for tagged routes.

Control-plane responsibilities (concise):
- Maintain per-route SLOs, current fidelity state, and link to responsible pool(s).
- Evaluate triggers on telemetry (metrics + traces) and compute action plan (which routes => which fidelity level).
- Apply routing changes via policy engine (tagging, route rewrite, model selector).
- Emit events: fidelity_change, spillover_start, spillover_end, rollback_attempt, cost_estimate_change.
- Persist decisions and allow manual override (ops) with audit log.

Policy pseudo-workflow (simplified):
1) For each route R monitor p95(R) and pool_util(P) where R runs.
2) If p95(R) > SLO(R) && pool_util(P) > threshold_high => compute candidate fidelity delta d=+1.
3) Check compatibility: model_variant_exists(R, level+d) && region_policy(allows_fallback).
4) If compatible => commit fidelity change for R and tag request traces with delta.
5) If not compatible => try spillover to region with spare capacity (see spillover algorithm).

Spillover algorithm (sketch):
- Rank candidate regions by: regulatory_compatibility, spare_capacity_score, added_latency_penalty, cost_delta.
- Prefer same-geo peer region with compatible model catalog.
- If no region meets min_latency_penalty threshold => prefer local degrade over long-haul failover for latency-sensitive SLOs.

Operational playbook (incident runbook notes):
- Detection: Alert on sustained p95 > SLO and auto-failures emitted by control plane.
- Triage: identify affected routes, their SLOs, and current fidelity state. Compare to expected cost impact.
- Containment: if spillover is causing cascade, revert non-critical routes to async mode (Level 4) and disable cross-region spillover for 5 mins.
- Recovery: restore full fidelity incrementally by route groups (low-risk first).
- Postmortem: annotate what triggered first fidelity change and whether cost forecasts were accurate.

Testing and validation matrix (must automate):
- Unit tests for policy engine: evaluate triggers at boundary conditions (85% util, p95=1.0xSLO, 1.1x, etc.).
- Chaos tests: region partition simulation where control-plane partitions for 60s, verify spillover ranking picks correct target and degrades only expected routes.
- Cost sim: run synthetic workload through fidelity ladder and validate per-token cost deltas match estimates.
- Smoke for private deployments: verify policy respects KMS/regulatory tags and never spillover off-network when policy forbids.

Edge cases and notes to self:
- Some customers demand data-residency: add 'no-cross-region' tag to route + model mapping and treat as hard constraint.
- Ensure canary: small percentage (1-3%) of traffic should be allowed to take lower-fidelity path early to validate quality loss before broad push.
- Beware cache-warmth effect: switching model family loses KV cache and can increase tail lat; incorporate cache re-warming hints (prefetch top-k prompts).
- Telemetry volume: fidelity churn can produce noisy events -> add debouncing window (default 30s) before committing further changes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact rollback window (N minutes) and slop parameters per customer tier (free vs enterprise).
- Add ML-driven decision scorer that predicts user-perceived quality delta for each fidelity step. Experiment: offline eval on historical prompts.
- Wire cost-estimate into billing simulation so product can opt-in to 'aggressive degrade' during peak hours.
- Draft UX copy for graceful placeholder messaging. Owners: Product (Priya).

Action items (short):
- [ ] Draft control-plane API for fidelity annotations (Diego) - JIRA-1301
- [ ] Implement spillover ranker with regulatory tags (Liam) - PR #467
- [ ] Create chaos test harness for region partition (SRE) - schedule Q1 run
- [ ] Eval offline prompt set to estimate quality loss thresholds (Applied ML)

Quick change log: 
- 2024-11-12: initial notes (Ava)
- 2024-12-05: added spillover ranking heuristics (Diego)
- 2025-01-18: included fidelity ladder cost deltas (Priya)
- 2025-03-10: expanded operational playbook and testing checklist (Ava)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc lightweight and link to canonical policy schema in Confluence. Remember to avoid shipping silent rollbacks without notifying product owners.
conclusion: This is a working draft intended to seed a small RFC and a control-plane spike. Goal for next quarter: prototype enforcement for one high-volume route and run chaos tests to validate rollback/rollback-safety.
